top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Washington promised the toughest sanctions in history against Iran, with details due Aug 24 — and on the same day President Masoud Pezeshkian said it was time to end the war 'as we are in a position of power and dignity'. China refused to help isolate Iran's economy, which is the test of whether any of it bites. The other pressure point was land and law: Israeli settlers moved back into Kadim near Jenin, 21 years after a previous Israeli government dismantled it, and five European and G7 governments demanded Israel drop its plans for 1,200 homes in the E1 corridor. Elsewhere the weather did the driving, from a Panama Canal transit cut to Sarawak shutting 591 schools in the haze. Watch Aug 24: if the sanctions text lands without Chinese cooperation, Tehran's opening is the more interesting half of the day.

stories.headline: US vows 'toughest sanctions in history' on Iran; Tehran threatens 'devastating' reply as Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war
stories.summary: Iran said on Aug 21 that its response to Washington's threatened sanctions campaign would be “devastating”, after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the day before that the US would impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling Iran's leadership. Bessent has promised details on Aug 24. The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, said the reply would come “across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace”, while parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Washington appeared to have concluded it could not win militarily. Separately, President Masoud Pezeshkian told a meeting of doctors it was “better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity” — the clearest signal yet from Tehran's civilian leadership. Both sides' characterisations of who holds the advantage are claims, not verified fact.

stories.headline: China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not solve the Iran conflict
stories.summary: Beijing publicly rejected Washington's push to isolate Iran's economy, saying sanctions and pressure are not a solution and urging a political settlement. The US had urged other governments, including China, to join the effort. China is Iran's largest oil customer, so its stance is the main practical test of whether the threatened measures can bite.

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill 17 across Kyiv and the surrounding region; Zelensky says Patriot shortage is costing lives
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, which hit blocks of flats and warehouses. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives, linking the gap to US stocks diverted to the war with Iran. Russia's defence ministry says it struck military facilities and warehouses. Casualty figures are from Ukrainian authorities and have not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Israeli settlers return to Kadim in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after it was dismantled
stories.summary: Thirty “pioneer families” arrived at Kadim, a settlement outside the Palestinian city of Jenin that a previous Israeli government evacuated in 2005 under its unilateral Disengagement Plan, after the current government overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attended an opening ceremony. All Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.

stories.headline: UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada demand Israel halt its E1 West Bank settlement project
stories.summary: Five key European and G7 governments issued a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, which critics say would sever the northern West Bank from the south and make a contiguous Palestinian state unviable. Israel's government rejects the criticism.

stories.headline: Hong Kong's Tiananmen vigil organisers convicted under the national security law
stories.summary: Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, were found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power over their role organising Hong Kong's annual vigils for the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown. Both face up to 10 years' jail; sentencing comes later. A third defendant, Albert Ho, 74, pleaded guilty in January. Amnesty International said the case relies on “vague, overly broad and arbitrary” definitions of subversion. Hong Kong banned the vigils in 2020, citing Covid-19 rules; they have never resumed.

stories.headline: Panama Canal cuts daily transits from 36 to 32 ships ahead of a severe El Niño
stories.summary: The Panama Canal Authority told shipping firms it will allow 32 vessels a day through from Sep 15, down from 36, phasing the measures in from Sep 3 to preserve water for human consumption and keep transits reliable. About 14,000 ships use the canal each year and it earns Panama roughly US$3 billion annually. The cut lands while shipping is already absorbing heavy disruption at the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: UK Met Office says this El Niño could be the strongest in living memory
stories.summary: Britain's national forecaster said the developing El Niño is on track to be the biggest and strongest in living memory, with knock-on effects on weather, food supplies and economies. A separate report on Aug 21 said El Niño rather than the recent earthquake is the bigger threat to Colombia's coffee harvest.

stories.headline: Eight killed in charter plane crash at a remote US Air Force site in western Alaska
stories.summary: A charter aircraft crashed near a remote military installation in western Alaska, killing all eight people on board, the US Air Force said. The cause is under investigation.

stories.headline: Japan executes man convicted of killing five in a pachinko parlour arson
stories.summary: Japan carried out the execution of a man convicted over an arson attack on a pachinko parlour that killed five people. Japan is one of the few developed democracies that retains capital punishment, and executions there are typically announced only after they are carried out.

stories.headline: Sarawak closes 591 schools for two days as haze pushes air quality to 'very unhealthy'
stories.summary: Sarawak's education department ordered primary and secondary schools across 10 districts shut from Aug 20, affecting 197,323 students, as the Air Pollutant Index hit “very unhealthy” levels — 239 in Serian by 11am on Aug 21. It is the second closure this month. Officials warn hazy conditions could persist through the weekend if biomass burning continues; smoke from fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan is the driver, and Singapore has begun seeing hazy conditions of its own.

stories.headline: China and Indonesia agree to deepen military ties and cooperate on minerals, energy and tech
stories.summary: Beijing and Jakarta agreed to step up defence cooperation and work more closely on critical minerals, energy and technology. Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest economy and a major nickel producer, and the agreement extends China's security footprint in a region where it also has maritime disputes with several ASEAN members.

stories.headline: Japan protests Russian missile tests off the disputed Kuril Islands
stories.summary: Tokyo lodged a protest after Russia held a rare missile test near the islands Japan calls the Northern Territories, seized by the Soviet Union in 1945 and claimed by Japan since. The test comes ahead of an expected Putin visit and follows Moscow summoning Japan's ambassador over the same islands on Aug 18.

stories.headline: US bond selloff resumes despite a Treasury intervention, as warning lights flash on the US economy
stories.summary: US government bonds sold off again even after the Treasury moved to steady the market, keeping yields elevated. A BBC analysis published the same day set out why the US economy is ringing alarm bells, pointing to the combination of a stalled bond market, tariff costs and the war-driven oil picture. Asian markets, by contrast, extended a rally as traders took comfort from the Treasury's pledge.

stories.headline: Imran Khan returned to prison after hospital treatment
stories.summary: Pakistan's former prime minister was taken back to jail after being moved to a private hospital for a medical examination, his party said. Khan has been imprisoned since 2023; his family and party have repeatedly raised concerns about his health and access to care, which the authorities dispute.

stories.headline: US and Canada 'very close' to a trade deal, Ottawa says
stories.summary: Canadian officials said the two sides are close to agreement as details of the emerging package began to emerge. Separately, China and Switzerland agreed a trade deal scrapping most levies between them, and Germany's finance minister said China is “not playing by the rules” — three strands of the same week-long scramble to re-cut trade terms around Washington's tariffs.

stories.headline: US charges woman over alleged IS-inspired plot to bomb the New York State Capitol
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors charged a woman with planning an Islamic State-inspired attack on the New York State Capitol building in Albany. The allegations have not been tested in court.

stories.headline: US-sanctioned ICC president warns of the 'demise of international rule of law'
stories.summary: Tomoko Akane, president of the International Criminal Court, said the sanctions Washington imposed on her and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye on Aug 18 point towards the collapse of the international legal order. The ICC has called the measures a “flagrant attack” on the court; the US says the sanctions respond to the court's actions against Israel.

stories.headline: Nigerian villagers bury the dead after an overloaded boat capsizes
stories.summary: Families in a Nigerian riverside community buried victims recovered after an overloaded passenger boat capsized. Boat disasters are frequent on Nigeria's inland waterways, where overloading and a lack of life jackets are recurring factors; official toll figures were still being updated.

stories.headline: Abbott to pay US$851.6 million to settle some preterm infant formula cases
stories.summary: The company agreed to the settlement to resolve a portion of the litigation alleging its specialised formula for premature infants caused a serious bowel disease. The agreement does not resolve all outstanding claims and Abbott has not conceded liability.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: An AI system running on cameras already fitted to buses will start catching bus-lane encroachers and road defects from the fourth quarter, part of a day in which the state pushed technology into a lot of everyday corners at once — a government chatbot in beta, a police block on a website falsely claiming foreign-ministry backing. The courts were busy and unhappy, with charges over $220,000 in alleged town council bribes and near-10-year sentences in a child abuse case. Heat and haze are now changing routines rather than just readings: mosques have shortened Friday sermons until further notice. The talk, meanwhile, was mostly about trust and its absence — a crocodile sighting that turned out to be a faked photo, now a police matter, alongside AI-cloned celebrities in TikTok ads. If you cook at home in Tampines, Punggol or Pasir Ris-Changi, the new $500 meal-credit scheme is the item worth checking.

stories.headline: PUB files police report after the Pandan Reservoir 'crocodile' photo turns out to be fake
stories.summary: National water agency PUB said on Aug 21 that the photograph submitted with a reported crocodile sighting at Pandan Reservoir on Thursday is fake, and that it has lodged a police report. Search operations have ceased and water activities — suspended on Thursday, which grounded the Singapore Rowing Association and Singapore Canoe Federation — resume from Saturday. Police confirmed a report was made and said investigations are ongoing. PUB said it takes a serious view of false information that causes public alarm.

stories.headline: Police block website that falsely claimed links to Singapore's foreign ministry
stories.summary: The Singapore Police Force issued an access-blocking direction under the Online Criminal Harms Act against the Global Asia Think Tank website, after MFA lodged a police report. Two other sites flagged by CNA — Great Vision consultancy and Afforesight — are believed to have been taken down by their owners. Global Asia had claimed it was supported by MFA and had worked with NUS's Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy and NTU's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies; MFA said it has never supported the entity and called the claims misrepresentations. CNA found the site's three most recent articles reproduced Taiwanese and American think-tank work word-for-word without credit.

stories.headline: LTA to use AI on existing bus cameras to catch bus-lane encroachment and spot road defects
stories.summary: An AI video-analytics system running on cameras already fitted to buses will be rolled out progressively from the fourth quarter of 2026 and extended to all bus routes by 2030, LTA said on Aug 21. It detects motorists who encroach into bus lanes or park illegally, plus road defects and non-compliant road works, and hit an average 90 per cent accuracy across the scenarios trialled. Senior Minister of State for Transport Sun Xueling said cutting bus-lane encroachment would reduce sudden braking by bus captains. LTA will also deploy automated safety announcements across the fleet from end-2027.

stories.headline: Friday sermons at Singapore mosques shortened because of the heat and haze
stories.summary: MUIS said Friday sermon sessions are being temporarily shortened from this week because of hot weather and the onset of hazy conditions, cutting the first sermon from the usual six to seven pages to under four. The change runs until further notice. The Meteorological Service Singapore expects below-average rainfall for the second half of August, daily highs of 33–34°C and up to 35°C on some days, and hazy conditions if fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan intensify. Singapore's 24-hour PSI was 60–74 — the moderate band — as of 1pm on Aug 21.

stories.headline: Over 3,000 lower-income residents in the north-east to get $500 in warm meals from food lockers
stories.summary: A programme launched by OCBC and the North East CDC on Aug 21 gives 1,000 households in Tampines, Punggol and Pasir Ris-Changi $500 in meal credits each — about 165 meals — redeemable at roughly 30 food lockers at or near the void decks of HDB rental blocks. It aims to provide 165,000 warm meals to more than 3,000 residents over a year from September, with eight halal-certified options at launch.

stories.headline: Singapore government beta-testing chat.gov.sg, an AI chatbot for official information
stories.summary: Chat.gov.sg entered its final pre-release phase on Jul 3, GovTech Singapore and the Public Service Division confirmed to CNA on Aug 21. It answers questions in everyday language in any of the four official languages, drawing on official websites, and uses a mix of the government's own tools and commercial AI services. Both agencies stressed it is not a replacement for helplines or officers who speak with the public.

stories.headline: Town council managing-agent employee charged over $220,000 in alleged bribes
stories.summary: A 63-year-old senior project manager at a town council managing agent, linked to three town councils, was charged with corruptly agreeing to accept about $220,000 from directors of a firm. Three other men were also charged over their alleged involvement. The allegations have not been tested in court.

stories.headline: Tradeluxury director charged with money laundering over the $32m luxury-goods scam
stories.summary: A director of Tradeluxury was charged with money laundering in connection with the Tradenation/Tradeluxury luxury-goods preorder scam. A woman was separately charged with allegedly handling $35,000 of ill-gotten gains from the ruse, which prosecutors put at about $32 million. The charges have not been tested in court.

stories.headline: 81 arrested in a four-day islandwide CNB drug operation
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau arrested 81 suspected drug offenders in a four-day islandwide operation, seizing drugs worth about $105,000. Officers also found katanas and knuckledusters in a Punggol flat.

stories.headline: Man who stabbed a priest during mass at St Joseph's Church jailed and caned
stories.summary: A 37-year-old Singaporean was sentenced to four years and three months' jail and nine strokes of the cane for stabbing a priest during a mass attended by around 900 people at St Joseph's Church in 2024.

stories.headline: Nearly 10 years' jail for man who abused primary school pupils, including forcing a boy to drink urine
stories.summary: A 31-year-old Singaporean was jailed nine years and 10 months, with caning, for abusing a six-year-old boy over 18 hours — making him hold a push-up position and drink his own urine. Two other boys, aged 10 and 11, were also abused.

stories.headline: MOM looking into claim that an airport wheelchair assistant had $5 docked for being 11 seconds late
stories.summary: The Ministry of Manpower said it is investigating claims that a wheelchair assistant at Changi Airport had S$5 deducted from their pay for clocking in 11 seconds late. The companies named in the circulating account are SATS and Aventa Services. Salary deductions in Singapore are governed by the Employment Act, which restricts what an employer may withhold.

stories.headline: HSA halts sales and recalls a Medicube cream suspected of containing a banned dye
stories.summary: The Health Sciences Authority said it has worked with the three companies marketing Medicube PDRN Pink Collagen Capsule Cream to suspend sales and recall the product, which is suspected of containing Sudan Red — a dye prohibited in cosmetics here under the Health Products (Cosmetic Products – ASEAN Cosmetic Directive) Regulations 2007 and flagged for potential carcinogenicity. HSA has opened an investigation and will test the product; consumers who bought it should stop using it as a precaution. Hong Kong Customs issued its own warning on Jul 24. Suppliers of such products face fines of up to S$50,000 and/or up to two years' jail.

stories.headline: Four operators approved to expand data centres, adding 200MW of new capacity
stories.summary: Singapore has allocated 200MW of new data-centre capacity across four approved operators, extending the controlled expansion that followed the lifting of the moratorium on new builds. Power and water constraints remain the binding limits on how much AI-era compute the island can host.

stories.headline: Singapore and Vietnam to hold their inaugural strategic dialogue on Aug 25
stories.summary: The two countries will convene a first-of-its-kind strategic dialogue on Aug 25, formalising a channel between them after upgrading ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Vietnam is one of Singapore's largest investment destinations in the region.

stories.headline: Apple impersonation scams cost Singapore victims at least $195,000 in crypto in two weeks
stories.summary: Police said victims lost at least $195,000 in crypto assets over a fortnight to scammers posing as Apple support, who convince targets their accounts are compromised and walk them through transferring funds. Separately on Aug 21, consumer watchdog CASE warned of phishing e-mails promising compensation payouts, and Mothership flagged a fake Mothership account promoting bogus S$139 Rolex watches.

stories.headline: TikTok ads use AI clones of Dewy Choo and Zhang Linghe to target Singaporeans
stories.summary: Advertisements circulating on TikTok use AI-generated likenesses of well-known figures including local personality Dewy Choo and actor Zhang Linghe to pitch products to Singapore audiences, without their involvement. The pattern mirrors the deepfake endorsement scams that have repeatedly used Singapore political figures.

stories.headline: Expect road and lane closures in Ang Mo Kio on Aug 23 for the National Day Rally
stories.summary: Traffic police flagged road and lane closures around Ang Mo Kio on Aug 23 for National Day Rally 2026. Drivers heading through the area that evening should plan alternative routes.

stories.headline: YouTube Premium prices rise across all Singapore plans
stories.summary: Google raised the price of YouTube Premium in Singapore across its individual, family and student tiers. It is the latest in a run of subscription increases landing on Singapore households this year.

stories.headline: Singaporean man, 56, jailed 14 days and fined for insulting Islam in Johor
stories.summary: A Johor court jailed a 56-year-old Singaporean for 14 days and fined him about S$2,192 (US$1,733) for insulting Islam during an incident in Johor Bahru. The case is a reminder that conduct crossing the Causeway is judged under Malaysian law, which treats religious insult as a criminal offence.

stories.headline: Debt collectors broke harassment law with threats and workplace visits, court rules
stories.summary: In a grounds of decision released on Aug 19, Protection from Harassment Court Judge Gregory Gan found employees of a licensed debt collection company breached the Protection from Harassment Act on four occasions while pursuing an alleged S$102,937 renovation debt — shouting insults at the debtor's home and visiting her husband's workplace, which had nothing to do with the debt. The judge said a debt collection licence is not “carte blanche” to break the law. The woman was granted a protection order; the identities of all parties were redacted.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on two missing teenage girls
stories.summary: Police issued separate appeals for a 13-year-old last seen near Westwood Avenue in Jurong West on Aug 19, and a 14-year-old last seen at Blk 183B Boon Lay Drive. Anyone with information is asked to call the police hotline on 1800-255-0000.

stories.headline: Nearly half of graduate industry trainees found jobs after finishing the programme
stories.summary: Close to half of participants in the Graduate Industry Traineeships programme secured employment after completing it, according to figures released on Aug 21. The scheme was set up to give fresh graduates workplace experience in a softer hiring market.

stories.headline: Motorcyclists hurt in a seven-vehicle accident on Sims Avenue
stories.summary: Two motorcyclists were injured in an accident on Sims Avenue involving five cars and two motorcycles. Emergency services attended; the circumstances are under investigation.

stories.headline: Father brings his daughter to meet the Roxy Square wanton mee uncle after the head-pat incident
stories.summary: Customers have been turning up at the Roxy Square coffee shop with gifts and children for the elderly stallholder who was shoved after patting a young customer on the head, in an attempt to encourage him to keep interacting with young children. One 40-year-old father brought his daughter specifically to reassure him. The stall has drawn steady queues since the incident circulated.

stories.headline: Actor Elvin Ng in tears as his 17-year-old dog is put down
stories.summary: Singaporean actor Elvin Ng, 45, said he had to euthanise his 17-year-old dog Bagel because of declining health, telling followers “I felt I could have done more”. The post drew a large response from local pet owners.

stories.headline: Singaporean in the Johor road-rage incident identified as a chicken rice restaurant owner
stories.summary: The 46-year-old Singaporean who fought with Malaysian police on the way to Woodlands Checkpoint has been identified as the owner of a chicken rice restaurant. He was granted bail of RM20,000 (S$6,301) and his case was adjourned to Sep 25. He has been charged with obstructing police and attacking a 30-year-old Malaysian woman, and did not indicate a plea.

stories.headline: Woman films herself collecting Hungry Ghost Festival offerings, says fruit is expensive in Singapore
stories.summary: A video of a woman picking up fruit left out as Hungry Ghost Festival offerings drew wide local discussion after she explained the cost of living was behind it: “It's not easy to work abroad. We have to save every penny.” The clip landed in the middle of the seventh-month period, when offerings are placed at void decks and roadsides across the island.

stories.headline: Taiwan deports Sri Lankan man to Singapore after he transited on a fake Canadian passport
stories.summary: A Sri Lankan man who used a forged Canadian passport while transiting through Taiwan was deported to Singapore. ICA confirmed he presented his Sri Lankan passport for immigration clearance here.

stories.headline: Teen seen with injuries after an alleged group bullying incident in Yishun
stories.summary: Footage circulating locally shows a teenage boy with injuries after a group allegedly assaulted him in Yishun; he showed signs of giddiness and left with the group despite a passer-by intervening. The account is based on a bystander's video and the circumstances have not been independently established.

stories.headline: Motorcyclist and pillion rider flee police, crash in Farrer Road
stories.summary: A 37-year-old motorcyclist with a 26-year-old pillion rider fled from police and crashed in Farrer Road, apparently hitting two small trees before striking a car. Officers found a vape and drugs at the scene.

stories.headline: Beatty Secondary students track down a wallet's owner using his NRIC
stories.summary: A man publicly thanked students from Beatty Secondary School who found his lost wallet and traced him through his NRIC to return it. The story circulated widely as a counterpoint to a run of grimmer local news.

stories.headline: Fake Mothership account pushes bogus S$139 Rolex watches
stories.summary: An account impersonating Mothership is promoting Rolex watches at S$139 — a scam. Mothership flagged the impersonation; the pattern matches the brand-impersonation ads that have proliferated on local social feeds.

stories.headline: Elderly woman injured in a fall on an escalator at Yishun's Junction 9
stories.summary: An elderly woman was taken to hospital after falling on an escalator at Junction 9 in Yishun. She is believed to have been pushing a trolley onto the escalator when she fell.

stories.headline: Milo Van sachets return with limited-edition Sports Day socks
stories.summary: Nestlé is selling Milo Van Sachets paired with limited-edition Sports Day socks, leaning on the nostalgia of the Milo truck that turned up at school sports days for generations of Singaporeans.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Iran's president publicly called time on the war while his armed forces chief promised a devastating answer to the sanctions Washington will detail on Aug 24 — a theatre looking for an exit and not yet agreeing on the door. In Ukraine the fighting stayed where it has been for weeks, in the air: Ukrainian authorities say 17 people were killed in the overnight attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, and Zelensky says an interceptor shortage he traces to the Iran war is costing lives. The traffic runs both ways, with petrol shortages now spreading inside Russia. The Israeli front barely moved militarily but shifted hard on the ground and in law, from settlers reoccupying Kadim to the sanctioned ICC president warning of the 'demise of international rule of law'. All three theatres are now being fought with instruments other than force, which is why none is closer to ending.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Ukraine's air defences, not the front line, are the binding constraint. Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, which hit blocks of flats and warehouses; Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage - which he links to US stocks going to the war with Iran - is costing lives. Russia's defence ministry says it struck military facilities and warehouses. No negotiating track is running: a senior Russian diplomat says Moscow will consider new peace ideas only on its own terms. The pressure is starting to run the other way too, with the BBC reporting petrol shortages spreading inside Russia after months of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure. Ukraine's domestic politics have quietened - the ousted defence minister's call for wartime elections has lost momentum and he is now fundraising in the United States - while Black Sea grain exports remain near zero.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
At least 13 people are killed in a Ukrainian drone strike deep inside Russia, according to Russian officials. The claim has not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia is using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine. Moscow and Pyongyang have not confirmed the claim.
Major Russian grain export terminals are hit in a Ukrainian attack on a Black Sea port, extending the campaign against Russian export infrastructure.
Russia dismisses the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, saying it sees no grounds for 'half-measures' that would give the other side a respite.
NATO jets shoot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the latest spillover of the air war into alliance territory.
Russia's defence ministry says its summer campaign has resulted in the capture of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine. Kyiv has not confirmed the claim.
Ukraine's General Staff says long-range strikes hit the Progress Rocket Space Centre in Samara, some 900km inside Russia, and a military airfield.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: For the first time, both capitals are talking about an exit rather than an escalation - but from opposite directions. President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'as we are in a position of power and dignity', the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the sanctions package he will detail on Aug 24 is meant to collapse the Iranian government. Iran's armed forces chief of staff promises a 'devastating' answer across land, sea, air and cyberspace, and its foreign ministry calls the sanctions 'economic terrorism'. China has publicly refused to help isolate Iran's economy, which is the main practical test of whether the measures bite. The Strait of Hormuz remains partially shut against a US naval counter-blockade, and the Houthis say they hit a Saudi airport and an Aramco facility; Riyadh has not confirmed damage.

timeline.event: Iran says a deal with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz is in its final stages.
Houthis reportedly kill six people in their first deadly attack since the start of the Iran war.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians. The Houthis have not commented.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the US will step up economic pressure on Iran, as two more ships are reported attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, according to Emirati state media.
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian', responding to Trump's threat to declare Hormuz US territory.
Yemen's Mocha port suspends commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's management says.
Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the coming sanctions will be the toughest in history, will 'squash' Iran's economy and that Washington intends to 'collapse this regime', suggesting the move lessens the need for new major military operations. No details of the measures have been released.
The BBC reports that Iran has for years proved adept at working around punishing sanctions, raising doubts about how much the threatened measures would bite.
The US Treasury issues fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, including re-designating it under a terrorism authority, in a move framed around the group's links to the Iranian government.
A new US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been on station for an extended deployment.
Yemen's Houthis say they targeted a Saudi airport and a Saudi Aramco facility. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any damage and the claim is not independently verified.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war: 'It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.' It is the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership that Tehran wants an exit, and follows its foreign ministry accusing Washington of 'economic terrorism'.

The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, says Tehran will answer new US threats with 'crushing, punishing and devastating responses' across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Washington appears to have concluded it cannot prevail militarily.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says details of the threatened sanctions package will be published on Aug 24, after saying the measures will be the toughest in history and are intended to collapse the Iranian government.
China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not resolve the conflict and urges a political solution, rebuffing Washington's request that Beijing help isolate Iran's economy.
A teenager pleads guilty in London over an arson attack on the offices of the Persian-language broadcaster Iran International.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: The contest has moved decisively onto land and law. Thirty settler families moved into Kadim near Jenin on Aug 20, reversing a settlement evacuation that a previous Israeli government carried out in 2005, with the finance and justice ministers present; separately the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada demanded Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 corridor, which the UN says would make a contiguous Palestinian state unviable. Israel's government rejects the criticism. The legal front is hardening in parallel: the ICC president, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warned of the 'demise of international rule of law', while Israel's military has confirmed its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in January 2024 and opened a criminal investigation. Strikes in Gaza continue; casualty figures there come from Gaza health officials and are not independently verified.

timeline.event: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers are killed by an explosion.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel rejects President Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza.
Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
Israeli forces block activists attempting to deliver aid to Palestinian families besieged by settlers at Qusra.
US officials say Washington wants Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settler siege at Qusra. Netanyahu has not commented publicly.

Israeli airstrikes on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people, Lebanon's health ministry says, in the deadliest day since the June truce. Israel says the strikes targeted Hezbollah.
A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: The UN's Ebola coordinator said on Aug 21 that Congo's outbreak is growing exponentially across an area larger than France, killing faster than the response can reach, with the funding pool weeks from running dry. The gap between what is confirmed and what is happening keeps widening — WHO's last formal bulletin logged 1,060 new confirmed cases in the 11 days to Aug 12, and the DRC's own reporting a week later was already well past it. The second obstacle is not epidemiological at all: 43 health workers have died of the disease, and more than 260 attacks on health teams in six months have burned ambulances and closed clinics. The 70,000 Ervebo doses allocated on Aug 20 are a real step but not a solution, since the vaccine is licensed against a different Ebola species. Risk outside central Africa stays low; watch whether the funding call is answered before September.

outbreaks.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: PHEIC in force since 17 May 2026; WHO says the epidemic is 'far from being under control'
outbreaks.scope_note: DRC confirmed cases and deaths only, reported by the DRC government on 20 Aug from data up to 19 Aug (ECDC). WHO's latest formal Disease Outbreak News (DON615, 14 Aug, data to 12 Aug) puts the cumulative confirmed total at 4,686 cases and 2,186 deaths across three countries — DRC 4,665/2,184 (case fatality 46.8%), Uganda 20/2 and one case in France, with two DRC-diagnosed patients treated in Germany. The newer DRC/ECDC figures are not yet DON-ratified. UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said on 21 Aug the death toll now tops 2,500 and the outbreak is growing exponentially.

stories.headline: UN says Congo's Ebola outbreak is growing exponentially as deaths pass 2,500
stories.summary: Senior UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis, speaking from Bunia on Aug 21, said more than 2,500 people have now died and the outbreak is spreading across an area larger than France, growing 'faster and wider than the Ebola response'. He said the existing pool of response funds will run out within weeks. Some 160 health workers have fallen ill and 43 have died; there have been more than 260 attacks on health workers in six months and eight have been killed, with ambulances burned and clinics attacked by residents who believe the outbreak is a hoax. Congo's 17th Ebola epidemic became its largest ever by case count in late July.

stories.headline: 70,000 Ervebo doses allocated to DRC, though it is unproven against Bundibugyo
stories.summary: The International Coordinating Group on Vaccine Provision approved 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine for the DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial and 50,000 for frontline and health workers — WHO and Africa CDC said on Aug 20. Ervebo is licensed against Zaire ebolavirus, not Bundibugyo: WHO states plainly that 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans', with early laboratory and animal data suggesting it may offer some protection. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo.

stories.headline: WHO's emergency committee reconvenes as the outbreak becomes the second-largest ever recorded
stories.summary: Opening the second IHR Emergency Committee meeting on Aug 18, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said almost 5,000 people had been infected and more than 2,300 had died across six provinces and 55 health zones, making this the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded and one 'moving faster than any previous Ebola outbreak'. He said the epidemic is far from under control and that responders are still playing catch-up. The DRC epidemic was declared a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May 2026.

stories.headline: WHO's latest Disease Outbreak News records 1,060 new confirmed cases in under two weeks
stories.summary: DON615, published 14 Aug with data to 12 Aug, reported 1,060 additional confirmed cases and 597 confirmed deaths in the DRC since the previous bulletin on 1 Aug. WHO attributes part of the rise to stronger surveillance and laboratory capacity but says most of it reflects genuine expansion. Cases now span 54 health zones across six provinces, with Ituri accounting for 85 per cent of confirmed cases; the newly affected Bas-Uélé province logged its first case in a patient who had travelled from Haut-Uélé. WHO assesses the risk inside the DRC as very high, high for neighbouring countries, and low globally.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch GitLab first: watchTowr is seeing in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-19478 within days of disclosure, having reproduced the bug in minutes — which is the real story about how fast AI-assisted attackers now close the gap. Microsoft separately disclosed a CVSS 10.0 Entra ID flaw that was exploited in attacks, already fixed server-side but worth a log review. CISA added six flaws to its exploited list this week, spanning TrueConf, MLflow, macOS, SharePoint, vCenter and Microsoft IKE, while Cisco shipped nine Crosswork and Secure Workload fixes with five scoring the maximum 10.0. The build pipeline took a hit too, with three Rust crates briefly carrying a script that disabled TLS validation. AI and assistant plumbing is now a standing category rather than a novelty. Three things: patch GitLab, audit the KEV list against what you actually run, and pin arrayref at 0.3.9.

stories.headline: CISA orders federal agencies to patch two actively exploited TrueConf Server flaws
stories.summary: CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 20 with a Sep 3 deadline for US federal civilian agencies. CVE-2026-72529 (CVSS 9.3) lets a remote unauthenticated attacker reaching TrueConf Server on 4307/TCP invoke an undocumented critical function and run an arbitrary script; CVE-2026-72530 (CVSS 9.5) lets an attacker who already has code execution inside the server's isolated environment escape the sandbox onto the host OS. BleepingComputer reports the Head Mare hacktivist group has exploited both since at least July 2026, swapping client installers for backdoored versions at Russian transport, energy, IT and software firms.

stories.headline: Microsoft says a maximum-severity Entra ID flaw was exploited in attacks
stories.summary: NVD scores the flaw 10.0: deserialization of untrusted data in Microsoft Entra ID lets an unauthorised attacker execute code over the network with no existing privileges and low attack complexity. Microsoft says the issue has already been fully mitigated on its side and that customers need take no action, and that exploit code is not publicly available. It disclosed four other maximum-severity issues affecting Azure Arc, Exchange Online and Apache Cassandra services in the same batch. Because Entra ID is the identity plane for most Microsoft 365 tenants, review sign-in and privileged-role logs even though the fix is server-side.

stories.headline: Cisco patches nine Crosswork and Secure Workload flaws, five of them CVSS 10.0
stories.summary: Five of the nine score the maximum 10.0 — SQL injection (CVE-2026-20030), missing authentication for a critical function (CVE-2026-20357) and external control of the file system (CVE-2026-20358) in Crosswork, plus improper access control (CVE-2026-20315) and improper authentication (CVE-2026-20317) in Secure Workload — meaning full compromise with no authentication or user interaction. Affected are Cisco Crosswork Data Gateway, Network Controller and Planning up to release 7.2.1, and Secure Workload 3.10 and 4.0 in both SaaS and on-premises form. Cisco found them in internal testing and says none are known to be exploited.

stories.headline: GitLab flaw exploited in the wild within days of disclosure
stories.summary: The code-injection flaw abuses a GraphQL directive to let unauthenticated attackers modify or delete publicly accessible GitLab projects and rewrite their contents, with no user interaction or special configuration. Security firm watchTowr said it reproduced the bug within minutes of disclosure and has since seen in-the-wild exploitation against its honeypot network. Fixed in GitLab CE/EE 19.2.4, 19.1.6, 19.0.8 and 18.11.11; affected versions run from 18.2. Patch now — a compromised repo is a supply-chain problem, not just an availability one.

stories.headline: Rust supply-chain attack plants build-time malware in crates with 245 million downloads
stories.summary: Malicious versions of three crates — arrayref 0.3.10, internment 0.8.7 and append-only-vec 0.1.9 — were published from a compromised maintainer account on Aug 20 and pulled within roughly 90 to 107 minutes each. They pulled in a `proc-macro1` dependency whose build script installed a certificate verifier that unconditionally returns success, disabling TLS validation, with a stage-2 implant that steals Chrome, Brave and Edge credentials from SQLite login databases and persists on Windows, macOS and Linux. Arrayref has 245,385,500 all-time downloads and 403 dependent crates. Nextron Systems reported it at 07:15 UTC on Aug 20; RustSec says there is no evidence any malicious version was consumed. Check `~/.cargo/registry/cache` and pin arrayref at 0.3.9 or earlier.

stories.headline: Suspected Russian hackers abuse Google OAuth and WhatsApp device linking to hijack accounts
stories.summary: Operators assessed as Russia-linked are walking targets through legitimate Google OAuth consent and WhatsApp linked-device flows to take over accounts without stealing a password or defeating MFA. Because the victim performs the approval themselves, the activity looks like normal account use in logs — audit linked devices and third-party app grants rather than relying on failed-login alerts.

stories.headline: AI-generated exploit scripts target Siemens S7 PLCs in US critical infrastructure
stories.summary: US agencies including CISA, the NSA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA have warned that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens programmable logic controllers, amid concern about intrusions at water treatment plants. The scripts lower the skill floor for operating against industrial protocols; the standing advice — get PLCs off the public internet and segment engineering workstations — has not changed.

stories.headline: Hackers abuse FTP server banners to deliver new Windows malware
stories.summary: A new Windows malware family retrieves its payload from text placed in FTP server login banners — a channel most network monitoring treats as benign metadata. The technique lets operators stage instructions without standing up obvious command-and-control infrastructure.

stories.headline: SickKids data breach exposes employee and job applicant information
stories.summary: Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children disclosed a breach affecting employee and job-applicant records. The hospital says patient care systems were not involved; affected individuals are being notified.

stories.headline: Critical NetScaler flaw can bypass authentication on Gateway and AAA virtual servers
stories.summary: CVE-2026-19490 lets a remote unauthenticated attacker bypass authentication when a NetScaler appliance is configured as an AAA virtual server or as a Gateway. A companion flaw, CVE-2026-19489 (CVSS 8.8), allows denial of service where SIP ALG is enabled on large-scale NAT groups. Citrix says neither is known to be exploited, but the Shadowserver Foundation tracks over 22,000 exposed NetScaler ADC instances and nearly 1,800 Gateways, and previous NetScaler auth bypasses were weaponised within weeks. Upgrade to 14.1-73.32 or 13.1-63.21 and later.

stories.headline: CISA warns of attackers exploiting a critical MLflow SSRF flaw to steal cloud credentials
stories.summary: Added to the CISA KEV catalog on Aug 19. The server-side request forgery flaw in MLflow before 3.15.0 lets attackers reach cloud metadata endpoints from the MLflow server and lift credentials and secrets — a direct path from an ML platform into the cloud account behind it. MLflow joins Ray and IBM Langflow as AI-stack software now on the KEV list. Upgrade to 3.15.0 or later and rotate any credentials the server could reach.
stories.source: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: isolated-vm flaw lets sandboxed JavaScript escape to the host
stories.summary: A weakness in the widely used isolated-vm Node.js module allows code running inside what is meant to be an isolated V8 context to reach the host process, opening the door to remote code execution. isolated-vm is a common building block for running untrusted user code and plugin systems, so the blast radius is anything that treats it as a hard security boundary.

stories.headline: Zimbra SNMP flaw exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.summary: Improper sanitisation of untrusted input during SNMP notification processing in the optional zimbra-snmp package lets an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary OS commands as the zimbra user. CERT Polska reported active exploitation and advised checking the past 30 days of logs for unexplained Zimbra service restarts and files created by the zimbra user. Fixed in Zimbra Collaboration 10.1.20, released Jul 20, 2026.
stories.source: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, CERT Polska, NVD

stories.headline: CDN Tsunami attack abuses HTTP/3 translation for up to 350x DoS amplification
stories.summary: Researchers showed that the way content delivery networks translate between HTTP versions can be turned into an amplifier, with a single small request producing up to 350 times the traffic against an origin. The abuse rides on ordinary CDN behaviour rather than a misconfiguration, so mitigation sits with the providers.

stories.headline: NASA AIT-GUI flaws could let unauthenticated attackers issue spacecraft commands
stories.summary: Flaws in NASA's open-source AIT-GUI, part of the AMMOS Instrument Toolkit used for spacecraft integration and testing, could let an unauthenticated attacker send commands. The toolkit is used outside NASA by smallsat and research ground-segment teams, which is where the practical exposure sits.

stories.headline: Elementor Pro flaw lets unauthenticated attackers upload PHP and execute code
stories.summary: A crafted multi-part upload bypasses validation and writes an executable PHP file to a publicly reachable directory on sites running Elementor Pro before 4.2.2. Exploitation requires a published Elementor form with a File Upload field and the multiple-file option enabled — off by default, which limits the population. Elementor Pro has more than 10 million active installs; version 4.2.2 shipped Aug 19 and no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported yet.

stories.headline: Cryptographic context injection could let a web page steal Grok chat data
stories.summary: A new attack class lets an attacker-controlled web page manipulate the cryptographic context of a chat session and read conversation data from xAI's Grok. It sits alongside the Copilot Personal one-click exfiltration research from earlier in the week as evidence that browser-integrated assistants inherit the browser's trust problems.

stories.headline: Zombie Card attack can revive expired Visa cards for contactless payments
stories.summary: Researchers found expired Visa cards can still be made to authorise contactless transactions under certain terminal configurations, meaning a card a consumer believes is dead can still move money. Issuers and acquirers, not cardholders, hold the fix.

stories.headline: Manic Android malware exfiltrates data from offline phones via nearby infected devices
stories.summary: Manic relays stolen data off a device that has no network connectivity by handing it to other infected handsets in physical proximity, defeating the assumption that an air-gapped or offline phone cannot leak. It matters most for high-risk users who deliberately keep a device offline.

stories.headline: ToxicPanda 2.0 and GoldDigger expand Android banking fraud with on-device execution
stories.summary: Both families have moved to on-device fraud, initiating transfers from the victim's own handset rather than exporting credentials — which strips away the device-reputation signals many banks rely on. Both have a track record of targeting Southeast Asian banking apps.

stories.headline: 40 malicious Firefox extensions pose as Web3 products to steal wallet secrets
stories.summary: Forty add-ons published to the Firefox extension store impersonated legitimate Web3 wallets and tools and harvested seed phrases and private keys. Anyone who installed a crypto-related Firefox extension recently should audit their add-ons and treat affected wallets as compromised.

stories.headline: Rogue ransomware affiliate poses as a recovery firm to intercept victims' payments
stories.summary: A group calling itself Ransom Busters claims to have hacked ransomware operators' servers and is approaching victims as a recovery service, asking for up to US$60,000. Whatever the truth of its claims, paying it carries the same risks as paying the original crew, with no guarantee it holds the data or keys.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Workers Spectre attack leaks a JWT from a co-located worker
stories.summary: Researchers extracted a JSON Web Token from a neighbouring tenant's Cloudflare Worker using a Spectre-style side channel, at about 12 bits per second. The rate is slow, but it demonstrates that co-located serverless workers are not a hard isolation boundary against a patient attacker.

stories.headline: Sakura Internet breach exposes data of up to 1.36 million accounts
stories.summary: The Japanese hosting and cloud provider said an intrusion may have exposed data belonging to as many as 1.36 million accounts. Sakura is a significant infrastructure provider in Japan, so downstream customers should review their own access logs rather than treating this as a single-company incident.

stories.headline: macOS, SharePoint, vCenter and Microsoft IKE flaws added to CISA's exploited list
stories.summary: CISA added four flaws to the KEV catalog on Aug 18: an Apple macOS improper-authentication issue (CVE-2026-65400, CVSS 9.8, fixed in macOS Sequoia 15.7.9 and Sonoma 14.x), a Microsoft SharePoint weak-authentication bypass (CVE-2026-55040, CVSS 9.1), a Broadcom VMware vCenter path traversal (CVE-2026-59310) and a double-free in Microsoft's Internet Key Exchange service extensions (CVE-2026-33824). This is the third SharePoint entry on the KEV list since mid-July — if you run SharePoint on-premises, assume it is being probed.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: Hackers compromise more than 14,500 Dahua devices via credential attacks and auth bypasses
stories.summary: Attackers combined credential stuffing, authentication bypasses and abuse of the vendor's peer-to-peer feature to take over 14,500-plus Dahua surveillance devices. P2P is what makes these cameras reachable without a port forward, and it is also what makes them reachable by the attacker — disable it, change default credentials and put the devices behind a VPN.

stories.headline: Clop-linked web shell decrypts credentials and maps engineering data in Windchill
stories.summary: A web shell tied to the Clop extortion group targets PTC Windchill product lifecycle management servers, decrypting stored credentials and cataloguing engineering data ahead of theft. Clop's pattern is to compromise a managed file-transfer or PLM platform quietly and monetise the data months later — manufacturers running Windchill should hunt now rather than wait for an extortion note.

stories.headline: Microsoft Copilot Personal flaws could let one click exfiltrate data from connected apps
stories.summary: Researchers chained flaws in the consumer version of Microsoft Copilot so that a single user click could pull data out of the apps the assistant is connected to. It is the same shape of problem now recurring across assistant products: the model's access to a user's mail and files becomes the attacker's access the moment prompt content can be attacker-controlled.
